title: Crash bars restored to 1 m and 3 m/s
summary: C15 (drop onto a guard, 1 m) and C16 (wall hit, 3 m/s) are judged in the strong filament (nylon-CF, strong_material) by CalculiX on the free drone, an elastic floor. The author had lowered them to 0.3 m and 1 m/s on numbers a 128-agent review then traced to the gate: CalculiX's multithreaded solver returning solutions out of equilibrium round sliver tets, single nodes at razor-sharp keep-out corners deciding the verdict, an analysis surface thinner than the print, and a drop pose in which the guard could not land first. With those fixed (single-threaded solve and an equilibrium check, keep-out edges rounded, stress averaged over 0.5 mm, one opening for every surface, the drop banked until the guard lands first), the frame takes 6.96 m and 2.76 m/s in PA6-CF (1.81 m and 1.24 m/s in PETG), converged on a finer mesh; the author restored the original bars.

rejected.value: a 0.3 m drop and 1 m/s wall floor
rejected.why: set on the broken gate's numbers (0.11-0.49 m, 0.29-0.78 m/s); the author restored 1 m and 3 m/s once it was fixed (2026-10-17)
would pass nylon-CF (2.76 m/s), but only by setting the bar to the result; 3 m/s is a jog, and the 8 % gap is real for P1's wall hits or a later design pass to settle
